properties.description:

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

- Showers and thunderstorms capable of producing flash flooding.
- Kingman, Colorado City, Valentine, Dolan Springs, Wikieup, Peach
Springs.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Pecos, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 26 at 2:08PM CDT until September 26 at 5:15PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Pecos County in southwestern Texas...

* Until 515 PM CDT.

* At 208 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Pecos County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Eastern Interior; North Central; Central Interior
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 26 at 3:05PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 305 PM AST, Doppler radar was tracking an area of strong
thunderstorms extending from Ciales eastward to Naranjito and Toa
Alta

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph. Funnel clouds and small hail are
possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Corozal, Naranjito, H. Rivera Colon, Galateo, Morovis, Orocovis,
Ciales, Toa Alta, Pajaros, Franquez, Barahona, Mucarabones, Rio
Lajas, Candelaria, Florida, Miranda, Barranquitas, Comerio, Pajonal
and Palomas.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 26 at 12:01PM MST until September 29 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive and long duration rainfall.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn areas, low-water
crossings, creeks, streams, washes and swimming holes. Larger
creeks and rivers may exceed bankfull. Flooding of paved roads and
highway underpasses will be possible. Unpaved roads could become
muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Low pressure will interact with tropical moisture from the
eastern Pacific. This could potentially produce numerous showers
and embedded thunderstorms, with heavy rain that will fall over
saturated soils and burn scars. This could lead to localized
flash flooding and rises on local rivers, such as the Little
Colorado River.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:

seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less

in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

County.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 11 AM EDT Monday, especially
around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Water is expected to come up through storm drains,
approaching businesses on Dock Street in Annapolis. Water is
expected to approach the Maritime Museum and begin to cover
Bowyer Road at the Naval Academy. Shoreline inundation up to one
foot above ground is likely in other low lying areas..

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one and a half to two feet above
normal. The next high tide at Alexandria is at 8:55 PM and 9:19
AM.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 26 at 1:56PM EDT until September 27 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 10 to 14 feet in the surf zone north
of Cape Hatteras. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents, large breaking waves expected, and strong
longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island. Beach hazard statement for longshore
currents and the high surf advisory is confined to beaches
north of Cape Hatteras.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until midnight EDT
tonight. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. NC-12 remains closed
from the Basnight Bridge to Rodanthe. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline and dune erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The next high tide is around 8 PM
tonight. The most likely time for strong rip currents to occur
is a couple hours either side of low tide, which will occur
around 2 PM Saturday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 26 at 12:18PM EDT until September 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Central and eastern Massachusetts as well as all of Rhode
Island.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of rain will continue across the region right through
Monday. Storm total rainfall amount of 2-4" are expected, but
localized 5-7" amounts are possible. If these higher amounts are
realized...the potential for both urban and small river/stream
flooding would increase. This is particularly true if these
localized higher amounts occur over a vulnerable urban center.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Delaware Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 26 at 11:51AM EDT until September 27 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of up to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.
Breaching of sand dunes is possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 26 at 5:16AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**NOLO REMAINS NEARLY STATIONARY SOUTH OF THE BIG ISLAND**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Big Island East, Big Island Interior, Big Island North, Big
Island South, Big Island Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala,
and Kona
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Haleakala Summit,
Kahoolawe, Kipahulu, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South,
Lanai Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley
South, Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward
South, Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai
Windward, South Haleakala, South Maui/Upcountry, and Windward
Haleakala

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 340 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 200 miles
south of Hilo
- 16.9N 155.5W
- Storm Intensity 105 mph
- Movement Stationary

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Nearly stationary, Hurricane Nolo is expected to strengthen into a
major hurricane as it turns westward and accelerates later today and
Sunday. Nolo is forecast to track northward early next week and weaken.
While the center will stay well south and west of the state, impacts
will extend far outside the center of Nolo.

Bands of intense showers and thunderstorms will bring an additional
6 to 8 inches of rainfall with localized higher amounts of 10 inches
to windward and southeast portions of the Big Island. This heavy
rainfall will cause significant, life-threatening flash flooding and
mudslides, particularly in areas of steep terrain. Isolated heavy rain
will spread to Maui, bringing an additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall
with locally higher amounts of 4 inches possible, especially over
steep terrain. Terrain-enhanced rainfall from outer rain bands may
also reach the rest of the state.

Tropical storm force winds and gusts continue across the Big Island,
and may reach hurricane strength today, especially over complex
terrain. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Maui County, where
tropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring due to terrain
enhancements. Strong, gusty winds will affect all Hawaiian Islands
through the weekend, and a Wind Advisory is now in effect for the
remaining Hawaiian Islands.

Swells generated by Nolo will bring dangerously large, rough surf and
severe rip currents, especially for southeast and east facing shores
of Big Island and Maui. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for
southeast and east facing shores of Big Island and Maui as well as
east facing shores of Molokai, Kauai and Oahu.

Tornadoes and waterspouts are possible near and over the Big Island,
primarily to the right of the track of Nolo.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island. Remain well guarded against
dangerous flood waters having possible significant impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,
arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island and portions of Maui. Remain well
guarded against locally hazardous flood waters having possible limited
impacts.

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across Big
Island and Maui. Remain well sheltered from dangerous wind having
possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Potential indirect impacts from the main wind event are also now
unfolding across the rest of the state. Remain well sheltered from
hazardous wind having possible limited impacts.


* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
southeast Big Island. Remain well away from locally hazardous surge
having possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across Big Island.
Remain well braced against a tornado event having possible limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a battery-
powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

Do not venture outside while in the eye of a hurricane as any
improvement in weather will only be temporary. Once the eye passes,
conditions will become life threatening as winds immediately return
to dangerous speeds, so remain safely sheltered from the storm.

Do not be a thrill seeker or risk your life for senseless photos or
videos.

Quickly move to the safest place within your shelter if it begins to
fail, preferably an interior room on the lowest floor as long as
flooding is not a concern.

If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional 1-3 inches, with locally

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for
moderate flooding rain
- The flooding rain threat has decreased from the previous
assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
moderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues
are possible.
- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area
vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action may result in serious injury or loss of life.

and rescues.

swifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,
especially in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams,
creeks, canals, arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken
foundations. Several places may experience expanded areas
of rapid inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and
poor drainage areas. Some streets and parking lots take on
moving water as storm drains and retention ponds overflow.
Driving conditions become hazardous. Some road and bridge
closures.

latest tornado situation.
- ACT: Move quickly to the safest place within your shelter
if a tornado warning is issued.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited

execution of emergency plans during tropical events.

off roads, and small boats pulled from moorings.

.Hurricane Nolo is generating a moderate swell that is producing
advisory level surf along east and southeast facing shores of the
Big Island, Maui, and Molokai that will maintain tonight and then
diminish on Sunday as Nolo moves westward away from the islands.
Strengthening trades also cause building surf which peaks tonight
for east facing shorelines and begins to diminish on Sunday.

* WHERE...East and southeast facing shores of the Big Island,
Maui, and Molokai.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate to high. Strong breaking waves and strong
currents will make swimming dangerous. Waves breaking in
channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.
properties.instruction:

go out.

properties.description:

portions of the Big Island and Maui.

* WHERE...Big Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, and Kahoolawe.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff. Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along

Big Island and Maui due to heavy rain from slow moving Hurricane
Nolo to the south of the Big Island. Areas most at risk for
flooding are the windward and southeast portions of the Big
Island where the ground remains saturated after recent rains.

heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Southwest Suffolk; Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 26 at 5:14AM EDT until September 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet and
locally up to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 14 feet in the surf
zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southwest Suffolk and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to major flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. There is an
elevated threat to low lying properties. Flooding could extend
inland from the waterfront and shoreline into areas that
typically don't experience coastal flooding. Flooding will
likely be exacerbated along north facing shorelines from wave
action, particularly for the barrier island from Atlantic Beach,
Long Beach to Jones Beach. This will result in numerous road
closures and cause widespread flooding of low lying property
including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Vehicles parked in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded.
Flooding in the most vulnerable areas may not totally recede
during the times of low tide.

* SHOREFRONT AND BEACH IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 6 to 10 feet
along with elevated water levels will result in widespread dune
erosion and beach flooding. Localized overwashes are possible
where dune structures are compromised, resulting in some
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective
dunes. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized
beach erosion. Life threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 26 at 1:53AM PDT until September 30 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf. There is a risk of moderate coastal flooding
especially Monday and Tuesday.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Malibu Coast and
Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
late morning high tide, including over beach parking lots,
bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal Flood Advisory products will
likely be needed for Monday and Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 26 at 3:08AM EDT until September 28 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7
feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Sunday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM EDT early this
morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6 to 8 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO; Dolores, CO; Gunnison, CO; Hinsdale, CO; La Plata, CO; Montezuma, CO; Ouray, CO; San Juan, CO; San Miguel, CO; Grand, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
